findings.title: `Integration.objects.get` in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` is missing `provider="github"` filter
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` (lines 478 and 494-496), `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` and `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` query the `Integration` table by `external_id` without filtering by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key` (`"github"`). Because the uniqueness constraint on `Integration` is `(provider, external_id)`, if another integration provider (e.g., `github_enterprise`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, etc.) already has an `Integration` record with the same numeric `external_id`, `Integration.objects.get(...)` will either raise `Integration.MultipleObjectsReturned` (causing an unhandled 500 error) or match the wrong provider's integration.

findings.title: Direct access to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise `KeyError`
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` at line 503, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes that every existing `Integration` without an `OrganizationIntegration` has `"sender"` populated in `metadata`. However, in `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration` (lines 376-377), `metadata["sender"]` is only set conditionally (`if state.get("sender"):`). If an `Integration` record was created via a previous pipeline installation (where `sender` is not in `state`) and its `OrganizationIntegration` was later removed, `integration.metadata` will not contain `"sender"`, causing an unhandled `KeyError` during re-installation.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` fails on OAuth state mismatch instead of testing 404 installation lookup
findings.body: In `test_installation_not_found` (lines 379-396), the test starts at `self.setup_path` without initializing the pipeline via `self.init_path` and passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline's signature (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). As a result, the request is rejected early in `OAuthLoginView` due to the state mismatch (`Invalid installation request.`), and `GitHubInstallation` / `build_integration` (where the mocked 404 response for `/app/installations/{installation_id}` is handled and raises `The GitHub installation could not be found.`) is never reached.
